title: Academic foundations
dek: Zong-Liang Yang's path began with rigorous scientific training.

title: M.S. in Meteorology
dek: Completed Master's degree in Meteorology at University of Melbourne.
narrative: This marked the beginning of Yang's formal training in atmospheric sciences, establishing the foundation for his future contributions to climate modeling.
mapCaption: Yang earned his M.S. in Meteorology from University of Melbourne.

title: Ph.D. in Atmospheric Sciences
dek: Earned doctorate from Macquarie University, Sydney, focusing on land surface processes.
narrative: Yang's doctoral research at Macquarie University established his expertise in land-atmosphere interactions and set the trajectory for his career in climate modeling.
proofPoints: Received Postgraduate Research Award from Macquarie University (1989-1992)
Member of Australian Meteorological & Oceanic Society (1990-1992)
mapCaption: Yang completed his Ph.D. at Macquarie University in Sydney.

title: University of Arizona
dek: Postdoctoral and research faculty position at University of Arizona.
narrative: Before joining UT Austin, Yang worked as a postdoc and then research faculty at the University of Arizona, further developing his expertise in land surface modeling.
mapCaption: Yang was postdoc and research faculty at University of Arizona.

title: Joining UT Austin
dek: Appointed to faculty at University of Texas at Austin.
narrative: In 2001, Yang joined the Department of Geological Sciences at UT Austin, beginning what would become a distinguished career spanning over two decades.
proofPoints: Appointed UT-Austin Representative to University Corporation for Atmospheric Research (UCAR) in 2001
mapCaption: Yang joined UT Austin faculty in 2001.

title: Noah-MP Land Surface Model
dek: Development of the Community Noah Land Surface Model with Multi-Parameterization Options.
narrative: Yang led the development of Noah-MP, a groundbreaking land surface model that would become critical infrastructure for weather and climate prediction worldwide.
proofPoints: Noah-MP adopted by NCAR Community Earth System Model
Integrated into Weather Research Forecasting model
Used by U.S. National Centers for Environmental Prediction
Implemented in the National Water Model
mapCaption: Noah-MP development at UT Austin became global infrastructure.

title: Jackson Chair Appointment
dek: Appointed to John A. and Katherine G. Jackson Chair in Earth System Sciences.
narrative: Yang's contributions to climate science were recognized with the prestigious Jackson Chair, one of the highest honors at UT Austin.
proofPoints: Joseph C. Walter Jr. Excellence Award (2007)
Co-Chair of NCAR Community Climate System Model Land Working Group (2008-2013)
mapCaption: Yang holds the Jackson Chair at UT Austin.

title: Hurricane Harvey Forecasting
dek: Yang's models proved critical in forecasting Hurricane Harvey's extreme rainfall and flooding.
narrative: The predictive models developed by Yang's team were instrumental in accurately forecasting Hurricane Harvey's devastating impacts, demonstrating the real-world value of his research.
proofPoints: National Water Model used Yang's Noah-MP parameterizations
Models accurately predicted extreme weather and water events
Research contributed to flood prediction and emergency response
mapCaption: Yang's models helped forecast Hurricane Harvey's impacts on Texas.

title: Elected AGU Fellow
dek: Recognized as AGU Fellow for exemplary leadership and outstanding scientific achievements.
narrative: Yang was elected as an American Geophysical Union Fellow, one of the highest honors in Earth and space sciences, recognizing his transformative contributions to climate modeling.
proofPoints: ISI H-index of 66, Google Scholar H-index of 81
Over $8 million in external funding as PI
16 PhD students and 3 MS students graduated
